core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Munim corresponds to the Arabic form مُنْعِم (Arabic root ن ع م (n-ʿ-m); مُنْعِم (Munʿim)). Its core sense is munim; benefactor, bestower of favours. faq.a: Munim is associated with the Arabic form مُنْعِم, whose core sense is munim; benefactor, bestower of favours.

faq.q: What is the origin of Munim?
faq.a: Munim is associated with Arabic. Munim is Arabic مُنْعِم (Munʿim) 'benefactor, bestower of favours', from the root ن ع م (n-ʿ-m). The source gloss 'Protector, Guardian' is unsupported and has been replaced with the lexical sense.
Yes — the underlying form مُنْعِم is Arabic.
Munim can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Munim should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. False

faq.q: What does Munim mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Munim is rendered منعم and carries the sense منعم، نعمت دینے والا.

faq.q: What does Munim mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Munim is rendered منعم and carries the sense منعم، نعمت‌بخش.
A romanized syllable approximation is mu-nim. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Munim?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Munim, munim. Script forms are منعم, مُنْعِم, मुनिम.

faq.q: Is Munim a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
